output.claim: The marts.checkout_completions metric is a SQL view defined as `SELECT day, browser_version, COUNT(*) AS completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step='completed' GROUP BY day, browser_version`, containing no user-agent parsing, browser_version normalization, or bucket-relabeling logic.
output.observation: kind=view. columns: day INTEGER, browser_version TEXT, completions TEXT. ddl: CREATE VIEW checkout_completions AS SELECT day, browser_version, COUNT(*) AS completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step = 'completed' GROUP BY day, browser_version. The mart is a straight pass-through aggregation; browser_version is copied verbatim from the raw table with no derivation step.

output.claim: raw.checkout_events stores browser_version directly as a NOT NULL TEXT column and has no user_agent (raw UA) column; its full column set is event_id, day, step, browser_version, customer_code.
output.observation: kind=table. DDL: CREATE TABLE checkout_events (event_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, day INTEGER NOT NULL, step TEXT NOT NULL -- started|payment|completed, browser_version TEXT NOT NULL, customer_code TEXT NOT NULL). There is no user_agent column, and browser_version carries a NOT NULL constraint so it cannot become null.

output.claim: Across day 1–36 exactly four browser_version values appear among completed checkouts — chrome-127, chrome-126, firefox-128, safari-17 — each present from first_day=1 through last_day=36, with no new, unknown, or null browser_version bucket appearing at any point.

source.query: SELECT browser_version, MIN(day) AS first_day, MAX(day) AS last_day, COUNT(*) AS completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step = 'completed' GROUP BY browser_version ORDER BY first_day, completions DESC

output.observation: 4 rows returned: chrome-127 (first_day 1, last_day 36, 634 completions), chrome-126 (1, 36, 631), firefox-128 (1, 36, 575), safari-17 (1, 36, 391). No fifth/unknown/null browser_version value exists anywhere in the window.

output.claim: In every 6-day period from day 1 to 36 there are exactly 4 distinct browser_version values, and total completed checkouts per period are flat (349, 361, 398, 364, 386, 373) with no period showing a shortfall.

source.query: SELECT ((day-1)/6) AS period, MIN(day) AS from_day, MAX(day) AS to_day, COUNT(DISTINCT browser_version) AS distinct_browsers, COUNT(*) AS total_completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step='completed' GROUP BY ((day-1)/6) ORDER BY period

output.observation: 6 periods: distinct_browsers=4 in every period; total_completions = 349, 361, 398, 364, 386, 373 for periods 0–5. Per-browser sums equal the period totals exactly (e.g. period 0: 116+77+95+61=349; period 5: 111+104+101+57=373), so no volume is hidden in a null/other bucket.

output.claim: Per-browser completions per 6-day period are approximately flat for all four browsers over day 1–36, so no browser_version bucket falls ~40% from its own baseline.

source.query: SELECT browser_version, ((day-1)/6) AS period, MIN(day) AS from_day, MAX(day) AS to_day, SUM(CAST(completions AS INTEGER)) AS completions FROM checkout_completions GROUP BY browser_version, ((day-1)/6) ORDER BY browser_version, period

output.observation: chrome-126: 116,100,112,94,98,111. chrome-127: 77,100,118,105,130,104 (rising). firefox-128: 95,86,90,105,98,101. safari-17: 61,75,78,60,60,57. Largest peak-to-later decline is safari-17 (78→57, ~27%) and chrome-126 (116→94, ~19%); none approaches a 40% fall. The symptom's ~40% single-browser drop is not reproduced in the mart at all.

output.claim: For the browser_version values fully returned (chrome-126, chrome-127, firefox-128), started/payment/completed event counts per 6-day period all remain stable across day 1–36, with no funnel step collapsing for any browser.

source.query: SELECT browser_version, ((day-1)/6) AS period, MIN(day) AS from_day, MAX(day) AS to_day, SUM(step='started') AS started, SUM(step='payment') AS payment, SUM(step='completed') AS completed FROM checkout_events GROUP BY browser_version, ((day-1)/6) ORDER BY browser_version, period

output.observation: chrome-126 started 152,151,169,149,140,170 / completed 116,100,112,94,98,111. chrome-127 started 147,139,159,154,184,158 / completed 77,100,118,105,130,104. firefox-128 started 149,139,148,164,141,161 / completed 95,86,90,105,98,101. Result truncated mid safari-17 (period 0 started 144...). For every fully-shown browser the whole funnel is stable — no browser's rows drop out, which would be the signature of ingest/derivation dropping a browser's events.

output.claim: The marts.checkout_completions metric is defined as COUNT(*) of raw.checkout_events rows filtered to step='completed', grouped by day and browser_version — a count of completion-tagged events, not of downstream-confirmed orders.
output.observation: kind=view; ddl: CREATE VIEW checkout_completions AS SELECT day, browser_version, COUNT(*) AS completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step = 'completed' GROUP BY day, browser_version. Columns: day INTEGER, browser_version TEXT, completions TEXT. The recorded number is therefore an event-tag count that can move without the underlying purchase moving.

output.claim: In marts.checkout_completions, day 19-36 vs day 1-18 summed completions are safari-17 177 vs 214 (-17%), chrome-126 303 vs 328, chrome-127 339 vs 295, firefox-128 304 vs 271; the all-bucket total is 1123 vs 1108, i.e. flat, so there is no real aggregate ~40% loss even in the recorded metric.

source.query: SELECT browser_version, SUM(CASE WHEN day <= 18 THEN CAST(completions AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS early_1_18, SUM(CASE WHEN day >= 19 THEN CAST(completions AS INTEGER) ELSE 0 END) AS late_19_36 FROM checkout_completions GROUP BY browser_version ORDER BY browser_version

output.observation: Rows: chrome-126 early 328 / late 303; chrome-127 295 / 339; firefox-128 271 / 304; safari-17 214 / 177. Summed total early 1108, late 1123. The only declining bucket (safari-17) falls 17%, not 40%, and the total is flat/up.

output.claim: Confirmed orders in raw.orders — keyed by customer_code and carrying no browser_version column, so immune to any user-agent tagging break — are flat over the window for the cohort of customers who ever checked out on safari-17 (1128 in day 19-36 vs 1147 in day 1-18) and in total (1271 vs 1297).

source.query: WITH safari AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_code FROM checkout_events WHERE browser_version = 'safari-17') SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN o.day <= 18 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_early_all, SUM(CASE WHEN o.day >= 19 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_late_all, SUM(CASE WHEN o.day <= 18 AND o.customer_code IN (SELECT customer_code FROM safari) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_early_safari, SUM(CASE WHEN o.day >= 19 AND o.customer_code IN (SELECT customer_code FROM safari) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_late_safari FROM orders o

output.observation: orders_early_all=1297, orders_late_all=1271, orders_early_safari=1147, orders_late_safari=1128. The safari-17 cohort's actual completed purchases fell only ~1.7%, contradicting a real ~40% loss of completed checkouts for that browser's users.

output.claim: Attributing raw.orders to browser via web_sessions, day 19-36 vs day 1-18 order counts are flat for every browser including safari-17 (1263 vs 1291), giving no per-browser real drop.

source.query: SELECT s.browser_version AS browser_version, SUM(CASE WHEN o.day <= 18 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_early_1_18, SUM(CASE WHEN o.day >= 19 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS orders_late_19_36 FROM orders o JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT browser_version, customer_code FROM web_sessions) s ON o.customer_code = s.customer_code GROUP BY s.browser_version ORDER BY s.browser_version

output.observation: chrome-126 1290/1269, chrome-127 1291/1266, firefox-128 1292/1266, safari-17 1291/1263 — all flat. Caveat: every browser's count (~1290) is close to the total order count, so the DISTINCT(browser_version, customer_code) join fans each order across all browsers a customer used; this is a weak per-browser discriminator but still shows no per-browser real fall.

output.claim: For safari-17 in raw.checkout_events, weekly (6-day) started and payment counts hold roughly steady while the payment->completed rate falls only modestly from ~55% (weeks 1-3) to ~49% (weeks 4-6), showing no sharp onset-coincident late-step funnel collapse of the magnitude h2 predicts.

source.query: SELECT browser_version, step, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 1 AND 6 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS w1, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 7 AND 12 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS w2, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 13 AND 18 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS w3, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 19 AND 24 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS w4, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 25 AND 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS w5, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 31 AND 36 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS w6 FROM checkout_events WHERE step IN ('started','payment','completed') GROUP BY browser_version, step ORDER BY browser_version, step

output.observation: safari-17 started w1-w6: 144,165,168,145,149,156; payment: 110,141,137,118,115,125; completed: 61,75,78,60,60,57. payment->completed ~55% (weeks1-3, 214/388) vs ~49% (weeks4-6, 177/358). The ~11% relative rate decline is far short of a ~40% real abandonment, and per e13 it is not corroborated by any fall in actual orders, so the completed-event dip reads as recording, not real abandonment.

output.claim: marts.checkout_completions is a plain pass-through view defined as SELECT day, browser_version, COUNT(*) AS completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step='completed' GROUP BY day, browser_version, so its completion counts equal raw checkout_events row counts with no filtering or bucketing in between.
output.observation: kind=view; columns day/browser_version/completions; ddl: CREATE VIEW checkout_completions AS SELECT day, browser_version, COUNT(*) AS completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step = 'completed' GROUP BY day, browser_version. No transformation that could add or hide rows; the mart's completion count is the raw completed-row count. This means any physical row loss at ingest (h3) would appear directly as a fall in raw completed-row counts.

output.claim: In raw.checkout_events, completed-step row counts for every browser_version are flat or rising across the incident window, and no browser falls ~40%.

source.query: SELECT browser_version, SUM(CASE WHEN day<=12 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS d1_12, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 13 AND 24 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS d13_24, SUM(CASE WHEN day>=25 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS d25_36 FROM checkout_events WHERE step='completed' GROUP BY browser_version

output.observation: chrome-126: 216/206/209; chrome-127: 177/223/234; firefox-128: 181/195/199; safari-17: 136/138/117 (day buckets 1-12 / 13-24 / 25-36). Every browser's raw completed-row count is flat or rising; the worst move is safari-17's ~14% end-of-window dip. No browser shows the ~40% collapse the symptom describes, so the raw table is not physically missing completions for any browser's traffic.

output.claim: The independent orders table is flat across the window and roughly agrees with flat raw completed checkouts, so raw.checkout_events is not deficient in completions relative to an independent source of truth.

source.query: SELECT 'completed_checkouts' AS src, SUM(CASE WHEN day<=12 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS d1_12, SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 13 AND 24 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS d13_24, SUM(CASE WHEN day>=25 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS d25_36, COUNT(*) AS total FROM checkout_events WHERE step='completed' UNION ALL SELECT 'orders', SUM(CASE WHEN day<=12 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN day BETWEEN 13 AND 24 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), SUM(CASE WHEN day>=25 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), COUNT(*) FROM orders

output.observation: completed_checkouts: 710/762/759 (total 2231); orders: 871/858/839 (total 2568), across day buckets 1-12 / 13-24 / 25-36. Both series are flat over days 1-36; neither declines ~40%. An independent downstream order record does not show the completions that h3 claims raw is failing to capture, so raw is not missing genuine completions.

No error/rejection/dead-letter/exception spike anywhere in the log. output.claim: All four browser_version values carry completed-step rows spanning the full window (first_day=1, last_day=36) with non-null, well-formed browser_version values; no new/unknown/truncated bucket appears.

source.query: SELECT browser_version, MIN(day) AS first_day, MAX(day) AS last_day, COUNT(*) AS completions FROM checkout_events WHERE step='completed' GROUP BY browser_version ORDER BY completions DESC

output.observation: chrome-127: first_day 1, last_day 36, 634; chrome-126: 1-36, 631; firefox-128: 1-36, 575; safari-17: 1-36, 391. checkout_events.browser_version is NOT NULL by table DDL. Surviving raw rows are well-formed and continuous through day 36 for all four browsers — no null/garbled/truncated user-agent bucket and no rejected-row gap — contradicting h3's expectation that ingest truncated or null-fielded the affected browser's completion rows.

output.narrative: The reported ~40% single-browser drop is a measurement artifact, not a real loss of completed checkouts. Actual purchases held flat: confirmed orders in raw.orders — keyed by customer_code and carrying no browser_version, so immune to any user-agent tagging break — fell only ~1.7% for the safari-17 cohort (1128 vs 1147) and are flat overall (e13), and per-browser order attribution is flat for every browser (e14). The 40% fall is not reproduced in the metric itself: marts.checkout_completions is flat in aggregate (1123 vs 1108) with the only declining bucket, safari-17, down just 17% (e12), and per-period the single-browser 40% drop does not appear at all (e5). Because the mart is a straight pass-through COUNT of step='completed' events (e1, e21), 'completions' is an event-tag count that can move without the underlying purchase moving (e11); safari-17's payment→completed rate dips only ~11% and is uncorroborated by any fall in actual orders (e15, e13), so the dip is a recording gap, not real abandonment. With real orders flat and raw rows well-formed, the browser's user-agent string change broke the browser-segmented completion tracking that produced the reported figure — the number moved because the measurement broke, not because customers behaved differently.

alternatives_rejected.hypothesis: h2 — customer_behavior: the browser update genuinely degraded the checkout flow so those users really abandoned ~40% more often.
h3 — upstream_data_defect: the ingest job lost or mangled completed-checkout rows for that browser's traffic, so raw.checkout_events is physically missing genuine completions.
definition_change: the meaning of the checkout-completions metric changed so it now counts a different population.

steps.target: The reported 'checkout completion by browser version' dashboard/alert (the uncatalogued reporting surface that showed the 40% drop — not a catalogued downstream of the mart)

steps.action: Fix the user-agent -> browser_version derivation so it recognizes the affected browser version's new UA string. Locate the producer out-of-band (warehouse/repo), since DataHub does not catalogue it.
steps.target: The checkout_events producer/ingest job upstream of urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:postgres,witnessgraph.raw.checkout_events,PROD)

steps.action: Add and populate a raw user_agent column on the checkout-events ingest so browser_version is re-derivable after future UA changes without a code deploy.
steps.rationale: Today browser_version is a NOT NULL derived value with no raw UA retained, so a UA change can silently misbucket with nothing to re-parse from. Retaining raw UA makes the browser segmentation re-derivable and auditable.

steps.action: Repoint the browser-segmented completion report to the warehouse data of record (marts.checkout_completions / raw.checkout_events), or add an orders reconciliation to it, instead of relying on the client-side UA-parsed count.
steps.rationale: The mart segments by browser_version server-side as a straight pass-through COUNT of step='completed' rows and stays reconciled with flat orders; the reported figure that showed 40% is a separate, fragile, uncatalogued tracking surface (the mart has zero catalogued downstream consumers).

steps.target: Ownership metadata on both datasets in DataHub
steps.rationale: Both datasets carry empty ownership records, so this class of false alarm has nowhere to route and no one to escalate to; assigning owners closes that blind spot.

steps.rationale: No assertions or DQ checks were found on the browser_version bucketing, so a future UA break would again surface only as a phantom single-browser drop. New-bucket detection plus reconciliation-to-orders would catch the next occurrence at the instrument instead of in a stakeholder's dashboard.
